job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: Cells are the fundamental building blocks of life, and their complexity is not determined by the size of the organism. An elephant is larger than a mouse not because its cells are bigger, but because it possesses a significantly higher number of cells. Every cell, whether in a tiny bacterium or a giant tree, contains genetic material to function. While eukaryotic cells store DNA within a membrane-bound nucleus, prokaryotic cells like bacteria keep their DNA in a specialized region called the nucleoid. Furthermore, energy production is a universal requirement for life. Both plant and animal cells contain mitochondria to generate energy through respiration, regardless of whether the plant cell also contains chloroplasts for photosynthesis. It is a common error to think that chloroplasts replace mitochondria in plants; in reality, plant cells rely on mitochondria to process the energy they create. Finally, the outer boundary of a cell is not a solid, static wall. The cell membrane is a dynamic, semi-permeable structure that actively regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, ensuring the internal environment remains stable. This membrane is distinct from the rigid cell wall found in plants, which provides structural support rather than acting as a simple, impermeable barrier.

items.evidence: An elephant is larger than a mouse not because its cells are bigger, but because it possesses a significantly higher number of cells.
items.q: Why is an elephant's body much larger than a mouse's body?
options: Its body is built from many more cells
Its body is built from much larger cells
Its cells grow bigger as the animal ages
Its cells are heavier because of more DNA
items.explain: An elephant is larger because it has far more cells, not because each cell is bigger.

wrong.why: thinks bigger organisms have bigger cells
thinks cells keep growing with the animal's age
links body size to the amount of DNA

items.evidence: While eukaryotic cells store DNA within a membrane-bound nucleus, prokaryotic cells like bacteria keep their DNA in a specialized region called the nucleoid.
items.q: A scientist studies a bacterium, which has no nucleus. What will she find about its DNA?
options: It lies in a region called the nucleoid
It is missing, as there is no nucleus
It is kept inside a membrane-bound nucleus
It is found only inside the mitochondria
items.explain: Bacteria have no nucleus, but they still keep their DNA in a region called the nucleoid.

wrong.why: thinks no nucleus means no DNA
thinks DNA can only be held in a nucleus
thinks mitochondria hold the genetic material

items.evidence: Both plant and animal cells contain mitochondria to generate energy through respiration, regardless of whether the plant cell also contains chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
items.q: A leaf cell has chloroplasts. How does it release usable energy from food?
options: Its mitochondria release it by respiration
Its chloroplasts release it by respiration
Its nucleus releases it by photosynthesis
Its cell wall releases it by respiration
items.explain: Plant cells have mitochondria for respiration, even when they also have chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

wrong.why: thinks chloroplasts replace mitochondria in plants
thinks the nucleus runs every cell job
mixes up the cell wall with other cell parts

items.evidence: The cell membrane is a dynamic, semi-permeable structure that actively regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, ensuring the internal environment remains stable.
items.q: How does the cell membrane help keep the inside of a cell stable?
options: It controls which substances enter and leave
It blocks every substance from entering
It lets all substances pass in freely
It makes energy for substances to move
items.explain: The membrane is semi-permeable and controls the movement of substances in and out, keeping the inside stable.

wrong.why: thinks the membrane is a sealed solid skin
thinks nothing controls what passes through
confuses the membrane with the energy-making mitochondria

items.evidence: This membrane is distinct from the rigid cell wall found in plants, which provides structural support rather than acting as a simple, impermeable barrier.
items.q: How is the cell wall of a plant different from its cell membrane?
options: The wall gives support; the membrane controls entry
The wall controls entry; the membrane gives support
The wall and membrane do the same job
The wall is flexible; the membrane is rigid
items.explain: The rigid cell wall supports the plant cell, while the semi-permeable membrane regulates what enters and leaves.

wrong.why: reverses the jobs of wall and membrane
thinks the wall and membrane are the same
